description: Cognito Authentication Bypass Attackers might attempt to bypass authentication by exploiting weak configuration in Cognito user pools, manipulating JWT tokens, or using stolen credentials. The current implementation uses email-based authentication with password policies, but could be vulnerable if not properly configured. An attacker obtains a valid JWT token through token theft or manipulation and uses it to access protected API endpoints, bypassing the Cognito authentication checks.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1550 - Use Alternate Authentication Material
recommendation: Implement additional authentication security measures

description: Transaction Data Interception Attackers might attempt to intercept traffic between components, particularly focusing on the communication between client apps and CloudFront, or internal communication between services. An attacker performs a MITM attack to intercept transaction data between the mobile app and CloudFront, potentially modifying transaction amounts or details.
references: recommendation: Implement additional data protection measures

description: SQS Queue Message Injection Attackers might attempt to bypass access controls or exploit vulnerabilities in the application to inject malicious messages into SQS queues, potentially causing processing errors or system overload. An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the transaction processor to inject malformed messages into the transaction queue, causing the budget analyzer to crash or process invalid transactions.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service

description: Privileged Data Access Abuse Privileged users with access to analytics systems might attempt to extract sensitive user financial data through direct database queries, EMR jobs, or by exploiting overly permissive IAM roles. A data analyst with EMR cluster access creates a custom job to extract and exfiltrate user transaction data from DynamoDB streams or RDS databases.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

description: DDoS and Resource Exhaustion Attackers might attempt to overwhelm system resources by generating a high volume of requests or exploiting resource-intensive operations in the application. An attacker uses a botnet to generate thousands of transaction requests per second, attempting to exhaust API Gateway limits or overwhelm the transaction processing services.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service

description: HTTP Request Smuggling Attackers exploit differences in how front-end and back-end servers interpret HTTP requests, potentially leading to request smuggling or cache poisoning. An attacker crafts specially formatted HTTP requests that exploit timing differences between CloudFront and ALB, allowing them to poison the cache or steal user sessions.
